ledger.note: 1958: Egypt sends troops into the Halaib Triangle in February. wars.outcome: Sudan seized Abyei in May 2011; South Sudan held Heglig from 10 to about 20 April 2012 and withdrew; Sudanese victory (infobox); eight agreements signed in Addis Ababa on 27 September 2012.

wars.outcome: Ongoing at the end of the dossier's span: by late 2023 the RSF held most of Darfur and most of Khartoum and took Gezira in December; in 2024 it took Babanusa's centre (January), Al-Fulah (20 June) and Singa (29 June, retaken 23 November) and besieged El Fasher from April.
wars.note: Events after 2024 (El Fasher falls 26 October 2025; the army retakes Wad Madani 11 January 2025 and Khartoum in March 2025; the RSF's Government of Peace and Unity, 2025) lie beyond the span.

certainty.note: The external frontiers follow colonial treaty and administrative lines; the exceptions are the Halaib Triangle (the 1899 line on the 22nd parallel against the 1902 administrative boundary), Abyei and Heglig on the South Sudan frontier, and the moving front lines of 1983-2005 and 2023-2024, which are soft.

notes: Cliopatria's Republic of Sudan includes South Sudan until 2013; its South Sudan row starts in 2014 although independence was 9 July 2011, so the dossier adds a 2011-2013 keyframe from the 2014 shape. The Cliopatria shapes follow the 22nd parallel in the north, so the Halaib Triangle (Sudan-administered 1956-1999 under the 1902 boundary) is drawn inside Egypt; the keyframes add it to Sudan for 1956-1999 and the ledger tracks the dispute (1958 crisis, Egyptian takeover 1994, Sudanese withdrawal January 2000, claim still open). Fix run of 2026-10-24 (after the review): the rebel-held land is now cut from the government keyframes, new keyframes 1989 (the SPLA's 'large areas', read from an undated sentence, confidence 1), 1997 (Central and Western Equatoria), 2000 (Halaib gone), 2005 (the autonomous south back in the shape), 2023 (RSF Darfur and Gezira) and a corrected 2024; the July 1992 offensive that took Torit is a gain from the SPLM (Eastern Equatoria, confidence 2) and the 2005 Comprehensive Peace Agreement returns the SPLM land (gain, not drawn as vassal). The 2024 RSF advances (Babanusa, Al-Fulah, Singa) and the army's retaking of Singa are events; the War in Darfur and the First Sudanese Civil War pages were opened and have war entries without contest events (the pages date no end to rebel control). The Sudan-South Sudan border conflict page (both URL spellings) would not load; the Heglig Crisis page was used instead. Pages silent on: the Kafia Kingi and Kiir Adem border areas, Abyei's boundary and the end of its contest (the Abyei page: both states still claim it, UNISFA there since 2011), the 1972-1983 Southern Sudan Autonomous Region (the First Sudanese Civil War page names a Southern Regional Government but not that name), the Al-Fashaga border with Ethiopia, the SPLA's extent before 1989, the date the army recovered each Sennar town in 2024. Rebel counterparts: sudan-people-s-liberation-movement (SPLM/A, 1983-2005) and rapid-support-forces (2023-) are dossiers of type rebel; Anyanya (1955-1972) held no mapped land and has no dossier. Counterparts without dossiers elsewhere: south-sudan (af-08), arab-republic-of-egypt and united-arab-republic (me-10). Gazetteer names wanted: Al-Fulah (place, West Kordofan), Abyei (place), Heglig (place), Torit (place, Eastern Equatoria), West Kordofan (admin1).
